topics.ai_primer:
# ASL 3.0 Primer for AI Agents
Execute: `asl run <file>` or `./<file>` | ASL VM Hermetic Sandbox | Zero overhead
File Triad: .skill (modular, auto-shadows to .md), .tool (MCP tool), .asl (native root)
Universal Code Tag: All code blocks use strictly ```asl

Structure of .skill / .tool:
```yaml
#!/usr/bin/env -S asl run
---
asl_version: "3.0"
name: "my-skill"
description: "Clear description for LLM dispatch"
interface:
  entrypoint: "run"
  protocol: "mcp-tool-v1"
capabilities:
  fs: ["./data"]
limits:
  max_fuel_opcodes: 1000000
---
# Semantic Instructions
Instructions for LLM.

```asl
match input.action:
  when "query":
    return {"status": "ok", "term": input.term}
  otherwise:
    return {"error": "unknown action"}
```
topics.content:
========================================================================
⚡ Agent Skill Language (ASL 3.0) - Language Reference & Cheat Sheet
========================================================================

ASL is an open specification where programming feels just like writing
Markdown. Your document IS your program — combining plain prose for AI
agents and humans with concise ```asl code blocks. Under the hood, ASL
transpiles AOT into hermetic, fuel-metered Starlark in RAM.

🚀 QUICK START:
  asl template skill > my-skill.skill    # Generate canonical skill template
  chmod +x my-skill.skill               # Make executable
  ./my-skill.skill                      # Run directly via universal shebang!
  asl run my-skill.skill                # Run via hermetic runtime

topics.title: YAML Frontmatter & Structure
topics.summary: YAML frontmatter specification, headers, interface and code blocks.
topics.content:
========================================================================
📝 ASL 3.0 Syntax & Frontmatter Reference
========================================================================

Every ASL document starts with YAML frontmatter between `---` delimiters:
- name: Identifier of the skill or tool
- asl_version: "3.0"
- description: Natural language description for LLMs
- interface:
    entrypoint: Function name to execute (default: 'run')
    protocol: Optional protocol (e.g. 'mcp-tool-v1')
- capabilities:
    fs: List of allowed confined filesystem directory paths
    domains: List of allowed HTTP domains
    env_keys: List of allowed environment variable keys
- limits:
    max_fuel_opcodes: Execution fuel limit (default: 1,000,000)
    max_heap_kib: Memory limit in KiB (default: 8,192)

Universal Code Block Tag: Use strictly ```asl for all executable logic.

topics.title: Declarative Semantic Rules
topics.summary: High-level pattern matching and declarative action dispatch.
topics.content:
========================================================================
🎯 ASL Declarative Rules Syntax
========================================================================

Inside ```asl blocks, declarative pattern matching executes deterministically:
match input.action:
  when "query":
    [guard len(input.term) > 0]
    return {"status": "ok", "term": input.term}
  when "health":
    return {"status": "healthy"}
  otherwise:
    return {"error": "unknown action"}

topics.title: The File Triad (.skill, .tool, .asl)
topics.summary: Differences and roles of .skill, .tool, and .asl file extensions.
topics.content:
========================================================================
🧩 The ASL Canonical File Triad
========================================================================

1. .skill: Modular, dual-audience (human/AI) document with automatic shadow markdown projection.
2. .tool: Pure MCP tool declaration for direct agent function dispatch without shadow projection.
3. .asl: Native root ASL module for deterministic backend workflows.

topics.title: Standard Library & Built-in Functions
topics.summary: Built-in functions, JSON encoding/decoding, and collection utilities.
topics.content:
========================================================================
📚 ASL 3.0 Standard Library & Builtins
========================================================================

Global Built-in Functions:
  len(x)                  - Number of items in string, list, dict
  range(start, stop, step)- Arithmetic sequence generator
  min(*args) / max(*args) - Smallest or largest element
  abs(n)                  - Absolute value of integer
  sorted(iterable)        - New sorted list
  enumerate(iterable)     - Yields (index, value) tuples
  zip(*iterables)         - Pairs items across sequences
  type(x)                 - Type name string ('string', 'int', 'dict', etc.)
  fail(msg)               - Terminates execution with error

Standard Modules:
  json.decode(str)        - Parses JSON string into ASL dict/list
  json.encode(val)        - Serializes ASL value to JSON string
  struct(**kwargs)        - Immutable record with dot access

String Methods:
  s.startswith(p), s.endswith(p), s.split(sep), s.join(list),
  s.strip(), s.replace(old, new), s.lower(), s.upper()

topics.title: Capability Context (ctx)
topics.summary: Object-Capability (OCap) APIs: fs, crypto, env, http, and fuel.
topics.content:
========================================================================
🔐 ASL Capability Context (ctx) API Reference
========================================================================

All I/O in ASL requires explicit capability grants in the frontmatter:

1. Filesystem (ctx.fs) [requires capabilities.fs]:
   ctx.fs.read(path)          - Reads UTF-8 text file
   ctx.fs.write(path, data)   - Writes UTF-8 text file
   ctx.fs.exists(path)        - Checks if file exists in confined roots

2. Cryptography (ctx.crypto) [Pure deterministic, zero grant needed]:
   ctx.crypto.sha256(data)    - Computes hex-encoded SHA-256 digest
   ctx.crypto.base64_encode(s)- Encodes string or bytes to base64
   ctx.crypto.base64_decode(s)- Decodes base64 string

3. Environment (ctx.env) [requires capabilities.env_keys]:
   ctx.env.get(key, default)  - Safely reads whitelisted environment variable

4. HTTP Client (ctx.http) [requires capabilities.domains]:
   ctx.http.get(url)          - Performs outbound GET request
   ctx.http.post(url, json=d) - Performs outbound POST request with JSON

5. Fuel Monitoring (ctx.fuel):
   ctx.fuel.remaining()       - Returns remaining execution opcodes
   ctx.fuel.spent()           - Returns spent opcode count

topics.title: The 7 Architectural Axioms
topics.summary: Inviolable principles governing safety, confinement, and determinism.
topics.content:
========================================================================
🏛️ The 7 Inviolable Axioms of ASL 3.0
========================================================================

1. Axiom 1 (Atomicity): .skill is self-contained with code, schema, and docs.
2. Axiom 2 (Zero Runtime Dependencies): No Python, Node, JVM, or OS daemons.
3. Axiom 3 (OCap Confinement): No ambient authority; all I/O gated via ctx.
4. Axiom 4 (Hexagonal Decoupling): Ports & Adapters; engines are swappable.
5. Axiom 5 (Deterministic Termination): Monotonic fuel metering prevents loops.
6. Axiom 6 (Static Prefix Invariance): 100% KV-Cache reuse on LLM inference.
7. Axiom 7 (Cognitive Boundedness): Files kept under 450 lines for instant AI ingestion.

topics.title: Best Practices & Daemon-Free Workflow
topics.summary: Guidelines for working efficiently without background services.
topics.content:
========================================================================
💡 Best Practices for Developers and AI Agents
========================================================================

1. Use Shebang on Line 1: `#!/usr/bin/env -S asl run` makes skills executable.
2. Verify Early: Use `asl check <file>` before deployment.
3. On-Demand Sync: Use `asl sync .` if background daemon is disabled.
4. Prefix Invariance: Consolidate static prompt blocks at top for 100% KV cache hits.
